text:
zuri (support): Hey team, customer Foodly reporting a big spike of 5xx/timeout errors this morning. They see ~15% of requests returning 504s and a bunch of slow p95s. Root says: 'sudden tail latencies, requests stuck in queue'.
arya (sre): tagging @mike @tasha — looks like classic queue pileup. Any alerting firing? Cloud metrics?
ingress-bot: Alert: hosted-gateway.queue_depth > 85% for cluster eu-west-1 at 2026-03-04T09:12:03Z. Spike duration 18m. Aggregated p95 latency up 4x.
mike (runtime): I'm seeing continuous batching backlog on the serving nodes taking longer to drain. Batcher counts spiked, concurrency hit tenant soft-limits. Likely long-running requests from Foodly (large context) + bursty fanout.
jen (foodly): Confirmed. We rolled out a larger prompt variant at 09:05 and then saw errors around 09:11. Some calls are heavy (>6k tokens). We thought the client would throttle but looks like many parallel requests.
zuri (support): Customer is escalated to SE team — they're worried about user impact. Asked for quick mitigation steps.
arya (sre): Immediate mitigations: 1) Apply tenant-level ingress throttle to cap concurrent in-flight for Foodly. 2) Temporarily route Foodly to fallback model with lower max_seq to reduce per-request cost. 3) Increase gateway queue capacity as emergency.
mike (runtime): Agreed. Also reduce continuous-batching window from 25ms -> 10ms for that cluster to avoid building large KV cache backlog. That will increase per-token cost slightly but reduce tail latency.
tasha (eng-platform): I can apply a per-tenant rate-cap via the routing policy. Doing canary now. Command: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/tenants/foodly/policies -d '{"ingress": {"max_inflight": 40}}'`
ingress-bot: Executed policy change: tenant foodly max_inflight=40 (applied to eu-west-1). Took effect at 2026-03-04T09:24:00Z.
jen (foodly): Thanks. We still see some 504s but lower now. p95 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s for a bit.
arya (sre): Good. Next, we need root cause. Mike: can you attach a timeline of queue depth, batcher backlog, and per-request token distributions for the interval 09:00–09:30?
mike (runtime): Pulling logs. Key observations: 1) Median tokens unchanged. 2) Top 5% requests have 10x tokens. 3) Batcher backlog rose as the continuous batching policy waited to assemble larger batches for throughput, but with long requests in-flight the effective concurrency decreased. Also saw a few stale KV cache eviction spikes.
zuri (support): Customer asked whether this is caused by model change or platform. They're wondering about billing impact — some of their jobs re-tried and doubled token consumption.
jen (foodly): We had no intentional retries. Some client-side timeouts might have retried. We're reviewing client SDK.
tasha (eng-platform): Action item: add short circuit/failfast at gateway for requests that would push tenant over a safe token-in-flight budget. This avoids long-tail single requests blocking the queue.
arya (sre): Agreed. Also note: our current per-tenant queue depth config is tied to cluster capacity but lacks token-weighting. Prototype plan: token-weighted slots where heavy requests consume more of the tenant's slot budget.
mike (runtime): Repro steps I ran in staging: 1) Spawn 350 concurrent light requests (<=200 tokens) + 20 concurrent heavy requests (~6k tokens). 2) Set continuous batching window=25ms and queue_depth_limit=500. 3) Observe tail p95 jump and a backlog where heavy requests occupy batcher KV for long durations -> later light requests time out.
Code/log snippet:
```
2026-03-04T09:11:05Z [batcher] queue_depth=621 backlog_ms=3420 heavy_inflight=18 light_inflight=326
2026-03-04T09:11:07Z [gateway] reject_rate=0.12 504_count=18
2026-03-04T09:11:12Z [runtime] kv_cache_evictions=73
```
zuri (support): That matches the customer's timeline. They also provided sample request IDs: req-FDLY-9342, req-FDLY-9348 that timed out.
arya (sre): For next steps: short-term: keep tenant cap and fallback model in place for 2 hours; medium-term: implement token-weighted queue slots and a failfast policy; long-term: smarter batching policy that prioritizes small latency-sensitive requests.
tasha (eng-platform): Filing a platform story: PLAT-4321 "Token-weighted tenant queue and failfast gating". I'll own the PR. ETA for patch: ~2 sprints.
mike (runtime): I'll open a runtime issue to add adaptive batch window per-tenant and an emergency drain knob. RUNTIME-987.
jen (foodly): Appreciate the quick action. Can you confirm whether we'll be charged for retried tokens? We're concerned about surprising overage.
zuri (support): I'll coordinate with billing team. Immediate note to customer: we'll issue credits for tokens consumed by retries attributable to platform-side 504s. cc @billing.
ingress-bot: Deploy: rollout/cluster-eu-west-1-batcher-config updated (25% -> 100%) at 2026-03-04T10:05:20Z.
arya (sre): Follow-up: collect the following artifacts for postmortem: customer request traces, gateway trace for 09:05–09:30, batcher backlog histogram, tenant quota config at time of incident, and model version mapping.
zuri (support): I'll collect customer transcripts and their SDK version. Jen, please send any SDK logs you have.
jen (foodly): Sent logs + request IDs in DM.
zuri (support): Current status: incident mitigated, foodly traffic stable, monitoring at normal. Reopening barrier-low; we'll prepare postmortem with timeline and code pointers.
mike (runtime): Adding suggested immediate config fix we applied to repo: `continuous_batch_window_ms: 10` for emergency profile.
arya (sre): Closing notes: No broader tenant impacts observed besides Foodly; but we should consider whether autoscaling thresholds should account for token-weighted concurrency rather than raw request count. Assign action owners in the postmortem.
zuri (support): Thanks all. I'll draft the incident summary and share in #incidents. :white_check_mark:
